lesson.title: React useEffect Hook Tutorial
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Set up counter component with useState
steps.instructions: From the empty folder, create a Vite React app (`npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react`), run `npm install`, render `<MyComponent />` in `src/App.jsx`, and start it with `npm run dev`. In `src/MyComponent.jsx`, import `useState` and `useEffect`, add `count` state, an `addCount` function and an Add button.

targets.caption: Initialize count state and addCount handler

explanations.topic: What useEffect does and its arguments
Three dependency array patterns for useEffect

hints: Have you initialized a Vite React project and rendered MyComponent inside App.jsx?
Import both useState and useEffect from 'react' at the top of src/MyComponent.jsx.
Use const [count, setCount] = useState(0) and update it with setCount(c => c + 1) inside addCount.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to export default MyComponent or import it in App.jsx.
Passing addCount() with parentheses to onClick instead of onClick={addCount}.
steps.code:
import React, {useState, useEffect} from "react"; function MyComponent() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); function addCount(){ setCount(c => c + 1); } return (<>

Count: {count}

); } export default MyComponent;

steps.title: Run useEffect on every re-render
steps.instructions: Add a `useEffect` hook in `MyComponent` whose arrow function sets `document.title` to show the current `count`. Leave out the dependency array so it runs after every render.

explanations.topic: Placing useEffect near the top of a component
Running side code on every re-render

hints: Where should hooks like useEffect be placed inside a function component?
Call useEffect with a single arrow function argument and no dependency array.
Write useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }); above addCount.
common_mistakes: Forgetting backticks around the template literal when interpolating ${count}.
Placing useEffect inside an event handler or conditional instead of the top level of the component.

steps.title: Run useEffect only on mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect so document.title only updates once on mount. Click Add in the browser to confirm the title does not change on re-renders.

targets.caption: Add empty dependency array to run only on mount

explanations.topic: Why an empty dependency array runs only on mount

hints: What second argument tells useEffect to run only once after mounting?
Add a comma after the effect callback function followed by an empty array.
Change the closing line of useEffect to }, []);
common_mistakes: Leaving out the comma between the callback function and the dependency array.

steps.title: Add count dependency and subtract button
steps.instructions: Add count to the useEffect dependency array in src/MyComponent.jsx so the effect runs on mount and whenever count changes. Add a subtractCount function and a Subtract button that decrements the counter.

targets.caption: Include count in the dependency array

hints: How do you tell useEffect to re-run only when a specific state variable changes?
Put count inside the square brackets at the end of useEffect, then add subtractCount and a Subtract button.
Use }, [count]); and define setCount(c => c - 1) inside subtractCount.
common_mistakes: Passing count without brackets instead of [count].
steps.code: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }, [count]); function subtractCount(){ setCount(c => c - 1); } <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>

steps.title: Track multiple dependencies with color state
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx create a color state initialized to "green", apply it to the count paragraph's style, and add a changeColor button toggling green/red. Include ${color} in document.title and use [count, color] as dependencies.

targets.caption: Add color to the useEffect dependency array

explanations.topic: Why missing color from dependencies leaves title stale
Why useEffect helps with code organization and cleanup

hints: If color is used inside useEffect, what else needs to be in the dependency array?

Add a second useState for color, apply style={{color: color}} on

, and add a Change Color button.
Update the dependency array to [count, color] so color changes also trigger the effect.
common_mistakes: Using single braces style={color: color} instead of double braces style={{color: color}} in JSX.
Forgetting to add color to the dependency array, leaving the title stale on color changes.
steps.code:
const [color, setColor] = useState("green"); useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count} ${color}`; }, [count, color]); function changeColor(){ setColor(c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green"); }

Count: {count}

steps.title: Create window size state and handler
steps.instructions: Replace the counter code in src/MyComponent.jsx with width and height states initialized to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight. Add a handleResize function that updates both and render the dimensions in two paragraphs.
hints: Which browser properties give the current viewport width and height?
Initialize two useState hooks with window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
Inside handleResize, call setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
common_mistakes: Misspelling innerWidth or innerHeight with lowercase w or h.
steps.code:
const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth); const [height, setHeight] = useState(window.innerHeight); function handleResize(){ setWidth(window.innerWidth); setHeight(window.innerHeight); } return (<>

Window Width: {width}px

Window Height: {height}px

);

steps.title: Attach resize event listener on mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, register `window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize)` inside a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array `[]` and log a message such as "EVENT LISTENER ADDED". Putting it in `useEffect` prevents registering duplicate listeners on every re-render.

targets.caption: Register resize listener inside useEffect on mount

explanations.topic: Why adding listeners outside useEffect causes 1000+ listeners
Why React StrictMode runs useEffect twice in development

hints: What happens if window.addEventListener runs directly in the component body on every re-render?
Wrap window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) inside useEffect(() => { ... }, []);
Pass handleResize without parentheses as the second argument to addEventListener.
common_mistakes: Calling handleResize() immediately instead of passing the function reference handleResize.
Omitting the [] dependency array, which still registers a new listener on every resize re-render.
steps.code: useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); }, []);

steps.title: Add cleanup and title useEffect hooks
steps.instructions: Return a cleanup function from the first `useEffect` that calls `window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize)` and logs `"EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"`. Then add a second `useEffect` with `[width, height]` dependencies that sets `document.title` to `` `Size: ${width} x ${height}` ``.

targets.caption: Return cleanup function to remove the resize listener
Update title when width or height changes

explanations.topic: When the useEffect cleanup return function executes
Using multiple useEffect hooks in one component

hints: How do you clean up side effects like event listeners when a component unmounts?
Return an arrow function () => { ... } from inside the first useEffect callback.
Add a second useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]); below the first one.
common_mistakes: Executing removeEventListener directly in useEffect instead of wrapping it inside a returned cleanup function.
Forgetting to pass the same handleResize function reference to removeEventListener.
steps.code: return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); }; useEffect(() => { document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; }, [width, height]);
